title: Hollerhorn Neapolitan Citrus Gin
about: Hollerhorn Distilling sits on a hillside outside Naples, the old grape village at the south end of Canandaigua Lake. Karl Neubauer, a Naples native and longtime custom home builder, studied distilling for some fifteen years before he and his wife Melissa opened in 2018, in a building Karl framed from timber salvaged out of collapsing barns. A fire in May 2022 destroyed the tasting room, but the stills and barrels survived, and the couple rebuilt with help from the whole valley. Karl works almost entirely with fruit and grain grown within a short drive of the distillery.

Gin sits on Hollerhorn’s list beside its rye vodkas, maple “tree spirits,” whiskeys and fruit brandies. Neapolitan is the word for someone or something from Naples, and the bottle appears in New York retail listings as Hollerhorn Neapolitan Citrus Gin. Hollerhorn’s own site describes only its other gin, Ginship, made in collaboration with Black Button Distilling in Rochester, whose second batch is coriander-forward with a hint of peach.

Neapolitan is a small local release, and Hollerhorn has not published its botanicals, base spirit or strength. What the name promises, and what Eden’s team finds in the glass, is a citrus-forward gin. Ask your server how it is being poured tonight.
